## Fade System Implementation

### **Fade Out to Black** (`fade_palette_to_black` @ 0x1b8b3)

The game uses a **palette manipulation** technique for fading:

```c
void fade_palette_to_black(void) {
  // Loop until all palette colors reach 0
  while (true) {
    wait_or_process_input();
    
    // Process all 256 palette entries (0x100)
    for (int i = 0; i < 0x100; i++) {
      // Decrease each RGB component by 1 (if not already 0)
      if (palette[i].red != 0)   palette[i].red--;
      if (palette[i].green != 0) palette[i].green--;
      if (palette[i].blue != 0)  palette[i].blue--;
    }
    
    // Apply modified palette to VGA hardware
    set_vga_palette(current_room_palette_ptr);
    
    // Check if all 768 bytes (256 colors × 3 channels) are 0
    bool all_black = true;
    for (int i = 0; i < 0x300; i++) {
      if (palette[i] != 0) all_black = false;
    }
    
    if (all_black) break;
    
    // Short delay (10000 iterations)
    for (int delay = 0; delay < 10000; delay++);
  }
}
```

**How it works:**
1. Decrements each RGB component of all 256 palette entries by 1 per frame
2. Writes the modified palette to VGA ports (0x3C8 for index, 0x3C9 for RGB)
3. Continues until all colors reach 0,0,0 (black)
4. Includes a small delay between frames for smooth visual effect

### **Fade In (No Dedicated Function)**

**The game does NOT have a dedicated fade-in function!** Instead, it uses:

1. **Instant palette load** via `set_vga_palette()` - simply writes the full room palette directly to VGA hardware
2. Room loading in `load_room_and_init_alfred()` calls `set_vga_palette(current_room_palette_ptr)` which **instantly** sets the palette

### **Special Case: Palette Cycling for Fade Effects**

For certain rooms, the game uses the `update_palette_cycling()` system in **Mode 1 (FADE)** to create smooth single-color transitions:

```c
// Mode 1: Fades a single palette entry between min and max RGB values
if (palette_cycling_config_ptr[1] == 1) {
  byte fade_direction = palette_cycling_config_ptr[0xb] & 0x40;
  
  if (fade_direction == 0) {
    // Fade down towards min color
    palette_cycling_config_ptr[2] -= step_r;  // red
    palette_cycling_config_ptr[3] -= step_g;  // green
    palette_cycling_config_ptr[4] -= step_b;  // blue
    
    if (current_color == target_min_color) {
      fade_direction = 0x40;  // Reverse direction
    }
  } else {
    // Fade up towards max color
    palette_cycling_config_ptr[2] += step_r;
    palette_cycling_config_ptr[3] += step_g;
    palette_cycling_config_ptr[4] += step_b;
    
    if (current_color == target_max_color) {
      fade_direction = 0x00;  // Reverse direction
    }
  }
  
  // Write to VGA hardware
  outport_byte(0x3c9, red);
  outport_byte(0x3c9, green);
  outport_byte(0x3c9, blue);
}
```

**Example:** Room 2 (McDowells restaurant) uses this for the neon sign fade effect.

### **Summary**

- **Fade Out**: Gradual decrement of all palette RGB values to black (1 unit per frame)
- **Fade In**: **No gradual fade** - instant palette load when entering rooms
- **Special Fades**: Palette cycling Mode 1 for specific visual effects (neon signs, etc.)
- **Hardware**: Direct VGA port manipulation (0x3C8/0x3C9)
- **Timing**: Software delay loops control fade speed

The asymmetry (gradual fade-out but instant fade-in) was likely a design choice to make scene transitions feel snappier when entering new rooms.
